# Quantum Polarization Loss Coding

> Quantum communication across labeled carriers with polarization-dependent attenuation and unknown axes that can change between coherence blocks.

The transmitter uses total spin zero. The receiver conditions on the erasure mask and measures the Schur spin to retain the multiplicity space. Match the common-filter promise and the accounting of every physical carrier before importing a formula. The finite singlet-restricted capacity, the all-encoder positivity criterion and the long-block all-encoder limit answer different questions.

## Science

- [README](README.md): question, four-carrier example and reading routes.
- [Model](science/model.md): flagged channel, admissible orientation sequences and entanglement-transmission criterion.
- [Schur receiver](science/schur_receiver.md): spin-zero encoding, exact channel reduction and two-survivor tags.
- [Chirality decision](science/schur_receiver.md#using-a-single-block-for-a-chirality-decision): one-block quantum memory, mask-only versus tagged readout, and the linked decision theorem.
- [Capacity](science/capacity.md): finite singlet formula, two-orientation converse and long-coherence rate.
- [Drift](science/drift.md): within-block perturbation bound and positive-rate concatenation.
- [Related work](references/RELATED_WORK.md): priors, inherited reductions and scope.
